identity_rules: Stable surface identities are references to editor, dashboard, chat, terminal section, workgroup, pane, session, and buffer owners.
Movement, docking, resize, close, reopen, and reload do not mint buffers, browser sessions, chats, terminal sessions, or PTYs.
Invalid or corrupt envelopes reset safely and record a reason; off-screen floating bounds recover to last_docked_host or home_main.

interaction_authority.state_rule: DOM and Slint controls project committed/draft model state; Pointer Events transactions preview locally and dispatch/persist once at semantic drop or resize end.
interaction_rules: Pointer capture, offset-preserving pickup, placeholder/reflow preview, edge-zone cues, cancellation, reduced-motion, and save-on-drop semantics are preserved from U10 vocabulary.
Four-edge scroll dissolve and the shared theme-aware resizer glow/recovery remain the common systems.
Web guarantees in-canvas floating and all four in-app docks; window.open is optional degraded behavior.

The 28 by 28 More options trigger sits immediately left of Theme and opens exactly Open Panel, Open Browser in Panel, a divider, Collapse Bottom Terminal, and Reset Layout; the Collapse row is a toggle (tweak wave 2026-08-13: runtime relabel to Expand Bottom Terminal while collapsed, one cmd.workspace_layout.set_collapsed with the negated current value per activation).
Open Panel and Open Browser in Panel are view-local disclosures; only Panel 1 through Panel 4 leaves dispatch commands. Collapse Bottom Terminal is never relabeled as Expand.

Reset is dual-surface (amended 2026-08-13): Settings > General & Appearance > Startup & Recovery and the top-bar Reset Layout row both dispatch cmd.workspace_layout.reset with no new command ID; the concept demo's post-reset reload is demo behavior only. Move or Dock remains retired and File Manager targeting remains File Manager-local.

Movement is direct manipulation from the top-right lines-only grip (tweak wave 2026-08-13; the corner triangle is retired): the held surface tracks the pointer one-to-one, the placeholder projects the TARGET geometry (fair share of the destination host; full width plus track thickness in row-axis docks) and re-seats only on a host or insertion-index change (one FLIP reflow wave per change, 16 ms stagger). A pickup still inside the source rect resolves to the source placement and a preview-expanded host never captures the hit-test for its preview growth. Preview never re-renders a surface subtree. Hosts carry visible-surface caps (left/right 3, top/bottom 2, floating 4, home_main uncapped) with announced host_full refusal; normalization spills overflow to home_main and never quarantines. Wave 3 (2026-08-13): target adoption has a two-frame hysteresis, mid-FLIP surfaces are excluded from hit-testing via data-pm-home-flip, auto-scroll re-applies only on actual movement, and the placeholder previews the proportional projected width mirroring normalizeMainRowBases; PM_EDGE band geometry defers during all Home gestures.

The centre-screen drop-target rail is retired. Drop targeting resolves surface-under-pointer, then outer edge band (the only route to a currently empty, zero-sized dock), then host-under-pointer, then home_main. Amended 2026-08-13: leaving the window resolves to invalid_target — floating is explicit-only through the Pop Out rows (editor panels, Chat, Dashboard) or the keyboard float key, and boot demotes persisted floating surfaces to last_docked_host with a storage.boot_demote_floating receipt. Wave 4 (2026-08-13): host targeting is latch-based and purely geometric - buildDockLatch freezes per-dock entry/exit bands at pickup (entry = committed dock rect plus the 28 px edge strip; exit = anticipated opened track plus 44 px slack) and elementsFromPoint is retired from drop-target resolution; one host transition and one track opening per approach into an occupied dock.
Loss of pointer capture is not a cancellation vector: live reflow re-parents projected items and drops capture. Escape, pointer cancellation and window blur are the cancellation contract.

Resize is adjacent-pair pixel transfer with fair-share minimum degradation, unified host bands, a floating bottom-right corner handle, commit without a full re-render, and the render-time no-dead-space invariant; the tweak wave adds row-axis dock two-axis sizing - within-row pair width transfer on the column dividers plus a full-width track handle writing the persisted size.cross_basis_px field (host-max semantics, host-band clamped, migrated from basis_px). A commit that moves zero pixels is a failure.
Keyboard movement on the grab handle is the accessible equivalent of the pointer gesture and carries the contract the retired menu rows used to hold, announced through a polite live region.

The grab handle is a small lines-only glyph (two diagonal strokes, no filled plate) over an 18 px clip-path hit triangle at the surface's TOP-RIGHT corner; the empty half falls through, focus renders in-glyph, and ARIA plus the keyboard grammar are unchanged. The surface kebab menus carry no Placement section or hint.

The base full-screen chat overlay is retired in PM7: every non-docked chat mode routes through PM_HOME_WORKSPACE.popOutChat into the single in-canvas float system (no scrim, title bar never covered, no second chat surface).

dock_right spans the full workspace height (grid areas 'top top right' / 'left main right' / 'bottom bottom right'); top and bottom docks end at the right column. Move Workgroup to New Section reseeds the vacated source section in the same commit (guidance state at the four-pane cap), and reset reconstitutes a live workgroup.

The surface options kebab is a vertical three-dot 16x20 control absolutely positioned at the surface's right edge directly below the grip, uniform across editor panels, Dashboard, terminal sections, and Chat (wave 3; no head-row kebab, and the stray terminal control strip is removed). Workspace spacing: 2 px vertical via --pm-home-pad-y/--pm-home-gap-y, 4 px sides. Wave 7 (2026-08-14): the kebab seats per kind - editor_panel top 10 px, dashboard top 5 px / right 13 px (clearing the grip's clip-path hit triangle) with a 34 px dashboard-actions margin; Chat is the exception - attachSurfaceControls skips and removes the T20 kebab for chat, the base chat header menu is Chat's single more-options, the chat-only Dock Back row is retired (grip-drag re-dock covers it), and Pop Out still routes through the T20 float guard with exactly one chat surface. Wave 8 (2026-08-15): the seat is derived from the glyph's INK, which sits at button-local top+10 (about 5 px of glyph-free padding above and below the dots), so the wave-7 tops are superseded - editor_panel top 6 px (ink at surface-y 16, one above the 35 px strip's label line at 17) and dashboard top 2 px / right 13 px (ink at 12, three above the 31 px header's title line at 15); right 13 px and the 34 px dashboard-actions margin are unchanged, and the grip hit-triangle concession is confined to glyph-free padding (about 50 px2 editor, about 4 px2 dashboard) so the dot column stays clickable on both kinds. The Chat clause is corrected: the T20 kebab stays skipped and removed for chat (the single-menu exception survives), but the Dock Back row is RESTORED for a floating chat - injected into the base .pm6-chat-more-menu rather than into any T20 kebab (see the floating-chat rule below).

Terminal empty-section guidance is truth-gated by #bottomPanel[data-pm-term-empty] stamped by the runtime projection, and restoreOwnerRefs repairs paneless pristine workgroup refs without dropping section records (wave 3).

Browser-in-panel deactivation is model-first (wave 4): deactivateBrowserProjection clears the persisted browser-active domain ref, restoreOwnerRefs can no longer resurrect it, and mountActiveBrowser enforces a single active tab and un-hides a chip-collapsed browser tab.

Home hosts lock horizontal travel (wave 7): overflow-x clip, overflow-y auto, overscroll-behavior none on .pm-home-host[data-pm-home-host] - the doubled attribute specificity is required because scroll-frost enrolment stamps the base pm6-bottom-scroll overflow rule onto hosts at runtime. Wave 8 (2026-08-15) supersedes the mechanism claim: overflow-x clip beside overflow-y auto COMPUTES to hidden (CSS Overflow 3 s3.1), so the hosts remained scroll containers whose scrollLeft still moved 12 px programmatically, and Safari 15 and earlier drop the clip declaration entirely. The overflow is removed at its three measured 1920x1080 sources instead - empty-dock padding 0 on .pm-home-host.pm-home-host-empty (the pm6-bottom-scroll stamp's padding var(--sm) floored an empty dock at 8 px on a 0 px track), a zero-extent guard in PM_EDGE layoutBands that hides all four 30 px frost bands when the scrollport measures clientWidth or clientHeight <= 0 (22 px), and extension of the row-dock last-sibling divider suppression to home_main (pairRow = rowDock || host === home_main), whose pairless last divider had no right-hand partner and overhung the host edge by about 11 px with its 16x56 grab-glow (12 px); dock_left and dock_right keep their last-surface dividers because there the handle drives the dock track via previewResize. Belt: overflow clip on BOTH axes for #pm-home-workspace, .pm-home-host-grid and #panel-dashboard.pm-home-owned (the dashboard panel was overflow hidden and silently held 26 px of scrollable overflow). The wave-7 host declaration scrollbar-color: var(--border-light) transparent is removed - it beat the scrollbar opt-in list's transparent idle ink and produced an always-visible thumb - in favour of ID-anchored zeroing, #pm-home-workspace .pm-home-host { scrollbar-width: none; } plus #pm-home-workspace .pm-home-host::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 0; height: 0; }, which wins by (1,1,x) specificity on every engine, order-independent, and is scoped to the host element so pane-internal scrollers keep their bars. Documented exception: inside the max-width 1320 px media block home_main returns to overflow-x auto so min-width floored pane content stays reachable, with the gutter still zero. The wave-7 diagnosis blaming the tab silhouette is retired: its flare box overhangs the START edge, which does not count toward scrollWidth in LTR.

A floating chat regains a Dock back row (wave 8, 2026-08-15). The base chat menu always renders its DOCKED variant - the variant is keyed by mount root id and T20 floats #chatPanel itself - so a T20-floated chat showed a useless Pop out window and no way back but the grip. attachSurfaceControls idempotently injects one button.pm6-chat-more-item carrying data-pm-home-chat-row="redock" (inline currentColor SVG, no emoji) before .closeChatBtn in .pm6-chat-more-menu; it displays only while surface.host === "floating", the base .popOutBtn row is hidden for the duration, both written if-changed, and exactly one injected row survives the chat engine's innerHTML rebuilds. wireActions' capture click listener handles [data-pm-home-chat-row] BEFORE its [data-pm-home-action] branch and calls moveSurface("chat", last_docked_host || "home_main"), deliberately without preventDefault or stopImmediatePropagation so the base delegated .pm6-chat-more-item handler still closes the menu with its portal animation. No new command id: moveSurface off a floating host emits the existing cmd.panel.redock, the same command the retired kebab's redock-surface action dispatched. Amends the chat float rule above (index 12) in spirit; that rule's single-in-canvas-float contract is unchanged.

retired_rows_2026_08_12.disposition: Retired with the per-surface Move or dock menu inventory. cmd.workspace_layout.move_surface is unchanged and is dispatched from home.<surface>.grab (pointer and keyboard) and home.drop_target.<host>.
